exposure: Reasons for seeking permanent contraception (e.g., not wanting children, fear of pregnancy/childbirth, current state of the world, environmental, medical)
Barriers to care (e.g., cost, inability to find a doctor)
outcome: Experience with seeking/obtaining permanent contraception (e.g., undergoing procedure, finding a doctor, facing barriers)
cohort: Adults in the United States, aged 18 years and older, who are childfree and seeking or have sought permanent contraception.
finding: Childfree individuals seek sterilization for various reasons and appear to have a low risk of regret, potentially lower than parous individuals.
cross-section timing: At the time of survey participation, reflecting current and past experiences with seeking and obtaining permanent contraception.
